blocks.text: Besides fossil fuels and their harmful effects, nuclear energy is an important and promising source of power that can help meet the world's growing energy needs. Nuclear energy is the energy released by the nuclei of atoms, either when heavy nuclei are split (fission) or when light nuclei are combined (fusion). These reactions release extremely large amounts of energy compared with chemical reactions.

Fission is the process in which a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 or plutonium-239 is split into two lighter nuclei, producing energy, neutrons and radiation. The neutrons produced can cause further fission in a chain reaction. The reaction between uranium-235 and a neutron is: U-235 + n -> Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n + energy.

Nuclear power plants use fission widely to produce electricity, getting a very large amount of energy from a small quantity of fuel. But it has serious drawbacks. It produces radioactive waste, which must be handled with care over a long time, and there is a danger of nuclear accidents, as at Chernobyl (1986) and Fukushima (2011); these accidents seriously harmed the environment and human health. Fusion, the joining of light nuclei, also releases a very large amount of energy.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: In 2011 a great earthquake and tsunami in Japan caused reactor accidents at Fukushima. More than 150,000 people were evacuated because of radioactive leaks, and the world became concerned about the safety of nuclear plants in disaster-prone regions.

blocks.alt: Top: a neutron strikes a uranium-235 nucleus, which splits into barium-141 and krypton-92 with energy; three neutrons fly out and each strikes another uranium-235 nucleus (chain reaction). The equation 235U + 1n -> 141Ba + 92Kr + 3 1n + energy is written below. Bottom: two small nuclei join into one larger nucleus, releasing energy (fusion).
blocks.caption: Nuclear fission and fusion (original diagram for topic 31.8).
blocks.long_description: One neutron splits one nucleus but releases three more neutrons, so the number of fissions can grow rapidly: this is the chain reaction. In fusion the opposite happens: small nuclei join into a larger one.

blocks.text: A solar photovoltaic (PV) system is a clean energy system. Its solar panels, usually made of silicon semiconducting materials, convert the energy of sunlight into electricity by the photovoltaic effect: light activates electrons in the material, producing direct current (DC). An inverter converts this DC into alternating current (AC), which can power homes, schools, offices and industries. The system also has batteries to store electricity for use at night or on cloudy days; they also help stabilise the voltage and supply surge current. Electrical accessories, wires, appliances and mounting structures make the whole system effective and safe.

blocks.alt: The sun shines on a blue silicon solar panel. An inset shows the cell layers: a (-) layer above, a junction (diode) and a (+) layer below, with freed electrons. A wire carries direct current to an inverter, which sends alternating current to a lamp for homes, schools, offices and industry. A battery connected to the DC line stores energy for night and cloudy days and steadies the voltage.
blocks.caption: How a solar PV system works (original diagram after Figure 31.7).
blocks.long_description: Light frees electrons at the junction between the two silicon layers, so the panel gives direct current. The inverter turns it into the alternating current that ordinary appliances use, and the battery covers times without sunlight.

blocks.text: Solar energy has key advantages over traditional sources of energy. It is environmentally friendly and renewable, so it helps in the fight against climate change and environmental pollution. Solar panels are also cost-effective in the long run, since they need little maintenance once installed. Energy shortages, high fuel prices and climate problems show that we need to switch to renewable energy sources such as solar, hydro and wind energy.
